claims_decomposed.text: Turkic damgalar (seals/marks) were used as identity markers to denote clan, family, or individual ownership
claims_decomposed.notes: Basic functional claim; widely assumed but needs primary source verification

claims_decomposed.text: Damgalar served as property marks on livestock, tools, and goods in pastoral Turkic economies
claims_decomposed.notes: Economic function; particularly relevant to nomadic/pastoral context

claims_decomposed.text: Some scholars argue damgalar were proto-writing systems or intermediate forms between symbolic marking and phonetic writing
claims_decomposed.notes: Central historiographical claim; needs academy positioning

claims_decomposed.text: Old Turkic runic writing and damgalar emerged as independent systems, not through direct transmission
Damgalar can be traced back to pre-Turkic (Scythian, Hunnic, other Inner Asian) marking systems
claims_decomposed.notes: Genealogical claim; requires deep chronological evidence

claims_decomposed.text: Damgalar symbols reflected totemism and clan-based social structure of Turkic societies
Kazakh, Kyrgyz, and other Turkic groups maintained distinct damgalar styles and meanings
claims_decomposed.notes: Regional variation; verifiable through ethnographic/historical records

claims_decomposed.text: Damgalar were predominantly used from medieval period through Ottoman era, with some continuous use into modern times
Ottoman administrative records documented damgalar usage for identification and property marking
claims_decomposed.notes: Archival claim; requires Ottoman record access

claims_decomposed.text: Damgalar symbols have been found on archaeological artifacts including textiles, metalwork, and pottery
claims_decomposed.notes: Archaeological claim; requires material evidence catalog

claims_decomposed.text: Some damgalar symbols appear morphologically similar to Old Turkic runic characters, suggesting possible influence or convergence
claims_decomposed.notes: Comparative morphological claim; needs visual analysis + expert interpretation

claims_decomposed.text: Western scholarship on Turkic damgalar has been limited compared to Central Asian scholarship, creating a knowledge gap
claims_decomposed.notes: Historiographical observation; meta-claim about scholarship distribution
